Dataset and code supplement to the scientific paper "Design and implementation of a location-agnostic and

control-oriented load surrogate model for wind turbines" submitted for review on Wind Energy Science journal.  

 

Authors: Adrien Guilloré, Andreas Vad, Filippo Campagnolo, Carlo L. Bottasso

Wind Energy Institute, Technical University of Munich, Germany

85748 Garching bei München, Germany

Contact: adrien.guillore@tum.de

 

Funding: This work has been supported by the MERIDIONAL and the SUDOCO projects, which receive funding from the European Union’s Horizon Europe Programme under the grant agreement No. 101084216 and No. 101122256, respectively.

 

 

Details on the method, implementation and validation of these load surrogate models can be found at: 





 Guilloré, A., Vad., A., Campagnolo, F., and Bottasso, C. L.: Design and implementation of a location-agnostic and control-oriented load surrogate model for wind turbines, submitted for review on Wind Energy Science journal. 

 Guilloré, A., Campagnolo, F., and Bottasso, C. L.: A control-oriented load surrogate model based on sector-averaged inflow quantities: capturing damage for unwaked, waked, wake-steering and curtailed wind turbines, Journal of Physics: Conference Series, 2767, 032 019, https://doi.org/10.1088/1742-6596/2767/3/032019, 2024.



 

This dataset and load surrogates were generated using the following open-source softwares and data:





 FAST.Farm with wake-added turbulence (Kretschmer, M., Jonkman, J., Pettas, V., and Cheng, P. W.: FAST.Farm load validation for single wake situations at alpha ventus, Wind Energ. Sci., 6, 1247–1262, https://doi.org/10.5194/wes-6-1247-2021, 2021.)

TurbSim (Jonkman, B. J.: TurbSim User’s Guide: Version 1.50, Tech. Rep. NREL/TP-500-46198, National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL), 1050 https://doi.org/10.2172/965520, 2009.)

Aeroelastic model of the IEA 3.4MW reference wind turbine (Bortolotti P, Canet H, Dykes K et al. IEA Wind TCP Task 37: Systems Engineering in Wind Energy - WP2.1 Reference Wind Turbines. United States: N. p., 2019. Web. doi:10.2172/1529216.) and its version for OpenFAST obtained from (https://github.com/IEAWindSystems/IEA-3.4-130-RWT)

FLORIS v4.5, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17186844, 2025.

TensorFlow python code suite, to build artificial neural networks for the surrogates (Abadi, M., Barham, P., Chen, J., Chen, Z., Davis, A., Dean, J., 970 Devin, M., Ghemawat, S., Irving, G., Isard, M., Kudlur, M., Levenberg, J., Monga, R., Moore, S., Murray, D. G., Steiner, B., Tucker, P., Vasudevan, V., Warden, P., Wicke, M., Yu, Y., and Zheng, X.: TensorFlow: Large-Scale Machine Learning on Heterogeneous Systems, https://www.tensorflow.org, software available from tensorflow.org, 2016).



 

 

This folder contains: 





"00_All_datasets_IEA_3400/IEA_3400 - Surrogate Training Validation Dataset_ Averaged Seeds.h5": the full post-processed dataset of 30783 points (each averaged over 24 seeds realizations for statistical convergence of the inputs and the outputs) built from FAST.Farm simulations using three IEA 3.4MW reference wind turbines, used for training and validation of the surrogates.

"00_All_datasets_IEA_3400/IEA_3400 - Surrogate Training Validation Dataset_ All Seeds.h5": the same as 1. including all non-aggregated turbulent seeds results for any seed-based analysis.

"00_All_datasets_IEA_3400/IEA_3400 - Farm Level Testing Dataset_ Averaged Seeds.h5": the full post-processed dataset of 735 points (each averaged over 24 seeds realizations for statistical convergence of the inputs and the outputs) built from FAST.Farm simulations using five IEA 3.4MW reference wind turbines, used for testing the surrogates on a new wind farm.

 "00_All_datasets_IEA_3400/IEA_3400 - Farm Level Testing Dataset_ All Seeds.h5": the same as 3. including all non-aggregated turbulent seeds results for any seed-based analysis.

"01_Main_recommended_surrogates": the trained and directly applicable load surrogate functions for each output channels of interest, as TensorFlow Keras models, and for each implementation environmment (DWM, Observers and steady-state wake models in Floris).

"02_All_surrogates_used_in_paper": This part will be completed upon acceptance and final publication of the paper in Wind Energy Science.

"03_All_training_routines_used_in_paper": This part will be completed upon acceptance and final publication of the paper in Wind Energy Science.

"04_All_evaluation_routines_used_in_paper": This part will be completed upon acceptance and final publication of the paper in Wind Energy Science.

"DescriptionOfChannelsInTheDatasets": A full list of the 323 dataset channels available (by columns), their description and units

"A_ReadDatasets.py": Python script usable to read the datasets and plot some sanity checks.

"B_Build_Load_Surrogates_with_grid_search.py": Python script usable to train the load surrogate functions as TensorFlow Keras models and evaluate their performances, including master grid search HPO. Tip: for the extensive results in the paper, this script was run heavily parallelized on a HPC using sbatch call job.

"C_Evaluate_Load_Surrogates.py": Python script to call and evaluate any load surrogate, to get estimate of DELs for any new set of inputs (local inflow quantities and local control set-points). 


 


This dataset and repository also represent the deliverable for MERIDIONAL D4.3: "Fast surrogate response models compatible with AI enabled flow models of WP3"
